text:
A: Hi. Sorry, I'm Lauren. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes. Hello, I'm Ioana.
A: Hi. Erm, where are you?
B: London. Burnt Oak.
A: Oh, okay. I'm Basingstoke.
B: I don't know Basingstoke. Only the name on the train.
A: That's sort of all there is, honestly. Roundabouts. Sorry.
B: Roundabouts is fine. What do you do?
A: I'm a vet nurse. Small animals. I'm on lates this week, so I'm a bit shattered, sorry if I'm slow.
B: Me also. I work evenings, cleaning in a school. So I understand. You looked tired in your photo, I thought, she works late, like me.
A: Ha, yeah. I thought the same about yours, actually. Not in a bad way.
B: No, it's true. Is that a cat at the bottom? Orange.
A: Yeah, Biscuit. He's a rescue. He came in to be put to sleep and I took him home instead. He's old now, he mostly sits on my keyboard.
B: That is a good story. You saved him. The caretaker at my school has a dog, very old also. He sleeps by the boiler and I give him a piece of my sandwich. I'm not supposed to.
A: What kind of dog?
B: I don't know. Brown. Grey face. Small legs.
A: Sounds like a good dog. Just maybe not too much sandwich, if he's old. Sorry, that's the nurse in me.
B: No, okay. I will give less. And the picture behind you, the cat, you made this?
A: Yeah, it's cross-stitch. I do animals mostly. It's quite calming after work, sort of counting the squares, if that makes sense.
B: Yes, it makes sense. I draw in a small notebook. Very bad, trees, mushrooms. But the looking is the point, not the drawing.
A: That's a nice way of putting it. Do you know mushrooms, then? Like which ones you can eat?
B: I'm learning. In Romania my grandmother knows all. Here I only look, I don't eat. I'm not brave.
A: No, I wouldn't either. We get dogs in who've eaten things in the woods and it's not good.
B: What do you read? I think you read, there were books in your photo.
A: Erm, mostly cosy crime. And fantasy, on my Kindle. I reread a lot. It's not very clever stuff.
B: Why not clever? If you read again, it means you love it. This is the best reason.
A: I suppose. I just know what's going to happen, so it's sort of safe.
B: Yes. Sometimes you need safe. After work especially. I read Chekhov on the bus, short stories, because I am too tired for a long one.
A: Is that, erm, like Russian?
